dedupe_keys.name: minerals for climate action the mineral intensity of the clean energy transition world bank 2020

description: This World Bank report estimates how much of each mineral the clean energy transition will need up to 2050. It models the mineral intensity of solar photovoltaic, wind, geothermal, concentrated solar power, energy storage and emerging technologies under International Energy Agency Energy Technology Perspectives scenarios, such as the 2 degree scenario, and IRENA REmap scenarios, and assesses recycling and reuse and the global warming potential of extracting and processing minerals. It was written by Kirsten Hund, Daniele La Porta, Thao Fabregas, Tim Laing and John Drexhage for the World Bank's Climate-Smart Mining Facility, supported by Anglo American, the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Rio Tinto and GIZ, and published in 2020. Coverage is global demand by technology and mineral. The report is available free as a PDF under the World Bank's rights statement. Findings: production of graphite, lithium and cobalt would have to rise by more than 450% from 2018 levels by 2050 to meet demand from energy technologies, while energy technology demand for aluminium in 2050 is only about 9% of current production. Caveats: results depend on scenario and technology assumptions that date from 2016 to 2017, and an annex lists the uncertainties. For simulation it supplies mineral intensity factors and demand paths for capacity planning and supply risk models of energy infrastructure build-out. It is related to the Critical Minerals Atlas record in this catalogue.
